text:
maria: heads-up — noticed a small billing cluster last night that looks like duplicate token charges from tool-calls when clients time out mid-stream. attaching quick log excerpt.
maria: ```
req=abcd-1234 parent=chat-xyz
stream: sent prefix tokens=118
client_disconnect at 0.75s (tcp reset)
server: retry-toolcall queued (same request id w/out idempotency key)
final tool response tokens=102
billing: charged tokens=220
```
jason: ouch. do we have the router + streamer traces correlated? sounds like both the prefix and the retry were billed.
li: I pulled traces — router accepted both because toolcall considered "in-flight" and we never persisted a per-request ledger entry until finalization. streamer has no dedupe by signature for tool calls.
kira: is this just tool-calls or streaming chat generation too?
maria: mostly tool-calls in this sample. streaming generative requests sometimes show similar patterns but rarer because we close prefix streaming earlier.
rob: quick question — did the client retry with the same client-generated id? if not, billing can't dedupe.
anna: logs show client retried after 1.2s with a new client id. network flakiness.
li: root cause summary: accept path increments ephemeral token counters for in-flight chunks; if the tool is retried by upstream (or client reconnects) we can double-count because finalization step doesn't know which ephemeral entries belong to a completed run.
maria: what are mitigation options?
jason: short-term: we can add a reconciliation job that detects pairs of toolcalls with identical parent+tool signature within 5s and issue credit if the first was short-lived (client disconnect). not ideal but quick.
li: long-term: change accounting to allocate tokens atomically on accept with an idempotency key recorded to durable ledger before executing tool. then mark consumed only once on final success. if retry arrives with same idempotency key, return cached result or dedupe charge.
kira: caveat: streaming partials complicate idempotency b/c legitimate partial + resume semantics exist.
rob: propose: 1) require idempotency for server-triggered toolcalls (internal router->executor) 2) for client-triggered streaming, emit a deterministic tool signature hash and use short TTL ledger entries so retries within TTL dedupe.
anna: also add telemetry: emit billing.debug events with fields {req, parent, prefix_tokens, final_tokens, client_close_ts} so we can reconcile and auto-credit.
maria: +1 for telemetry. we should also mark affected customers and proactively credit until fix lands. @billing ?
billing-bot: Created ticket BILL-7832 and flagged high-priority; assigned to @billing-team.
deploy-bot: Patch branch created: platform/patch/toolcall-ledger-ttl. Includes reconciliation job and extra billing.events.
li: rough plan + owners: li -> ledger durability change (epic), jason -> reconciliation job & credit automation, anna -> telemetry/events, kira -> UX change to require client idempotency header in streaming SDKs.
kira: SDK change note: we'll add a header X-Redwood-Idempotency but keep fallback behavior for older clients for 30d.
rob: risk: ledger change touches hot path; need perf benchmark. propose canary to 10% traffic on Dedicated before broad rollout.
maria: canary + metric checks: token-charge-per-request, dup-charge-rate, p50 token latency.
jason: I'll own canary plan and fallout alerting.
anna: I'll add a dashboard tile to console: "duplicate charge rate" by region + model so we can monitor.
li: temp reconcile query we can run daily: SELECT sum(prefix_tokens+final_tokens) - billed_tokens FROM toolcall_events WHERE parent...
maria: thanks team — adding follow-up items to the incident doc and scheduling a 30-min sync at 14:00 to finalize owners. I'm picking up the customer credits until automation is live. :thumbsup:
rob: sgtm
kira: i'll update SDK PR today
jason: starting canary config now, will ping when live.
maria: tagging for visibility @eng-platform @billing.
